correctness.rationale: The eight token types give two branch blocks that are incidence graphs of K_a and K_b, and a mixed block with left shore L consisting of opposite-center/leaf pairs and right shore consisting of mixed-leaf pairs and the double-center pair XY. Within a branch of size t, the minimum cover and maximum matching are min(t, binom(t,2)); for t≥3 the cyclic successor edges match the t leaf-vertices. Omitting p leaf-vertices forces p(2t−p−1)/2 edge-vertices, so t≥4 makes every p>0 strictly worse; t=3 ties only at p=3, and t=1,2 give the unique empty or sole edge-vertex cover. For a,b≥2 one can match L into mixed-leaf pairs alone: these are incidence edges of K_(a,b), which has a spanning unicyclic subgraph, so assign vertices one outgoing edge by orienting the cycle and directing off-cycle paths toward it. When a=1, match the b opposite-center pairs on the b side to their distinct mixed-leaf neighbors and the remaining vertex to XY, or symmetrically. Combining block matchings and the covers with L proves the exact scalar formulas. In every global minimum cover the restriction to each block is minimum. Omitting any L-vertices when a,b≥2 forces at least that many distinct mixed-leaf vertices plus the extra XY. For a singleton branch, its empty incidence cover forces the corresponding L-vertex via the interblock edge; omitting any other L-vertex then likewise forces its distinct mixed-leaf match and XY. The mixed block by itself need not have a unique cover at this boundary, which is why the interblock edge is essential. All remaining choices are independent because interblock edges meet L. Taking complements yields the claimed mandatory configurations, branch-size-three choices and exact number of maxima. Fresh exact optimizer and matching checks corroborated all nine pairs 1≤a,b≤3, and (4,1) with 21 vertices, alpha 12, matching/cover 9 and one maximum independent set.
